claims.text: Phase stability in high-temperature disordered BCC Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by the kinetics of Al-induced local chemical ordering.
Al-induced local ordering reduces local configurational entropy.
Local ordering creates chemical inhomogeneities that act as nucleation sites for secondary-phase precipitation.
The homogenized high-temperature state of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is disordered BCC.
Isothermal annealing between 650 and 750°C promotes kinetically driven ordering and phase separation relative to rapid quenching.
Rapid quenching preserves the high-temperature disordered BCC state.
The relevant structural mediator is localized B2-type chemical ordering.
Localized B2-type ordering occurs particularly through formation of Al-rich clusters.
Al-rich, B2-type ordered regions mediate nucleation of sigma or FCC precipitates.
Al induces local chemical ordering within the BCC matrix upon cooling.
Ordering-induced chemical inhomogeneities lower the energy barrier for phase separation.
High-temperature BCC stability is entropy driven, whereas low-temperature ordering destabilizes that state.
Atomic diffusion and ordering rates govern the onset of phase transformation.
Annealing will produce B2-type ordered domains with time- and temperature-dependent evolution.
Ordered regions will initially become detectable around 700°C.
Secondary sigma or FCC phases will appear only after B2-type ordered regions form and a critical time-temperature condition is exceeded.
Below a time-temperature threshold, the BCC matrix remains metastable with minimal local ordering.
Above the time-temperature threshold, significant B2-type ordering and subsequent phase separation occur.
